support.openTitle: Open Markdown without changing the original
support.openBody: Open local .md or .markdown files by picker or drag-and-drop, or continue from supported public GitHub Markdown through the extension.
support.openSafety: Source-safe review happens in the browser and never writes back to the original. Save reviewed copy creates a separate Obsidian-ready .md successor and carries annotations forward.
support.openVersions: Version history lets you reopen browser-local successors created from the current document lineage.
support.storageBody: Saved annotations and imported GitHub document copies use browser site data, not ordinary browser cache. Local files remain session inputs; wowMD stores their annotations by document fingerprint.
support.storageRisk: Clearing site data, private browsing, another browser, profile, or device, and storage eviction can remove browser-local work. Unsaved toolbar drafts can also be lost after refresh or crash.
support.storageProtect: Export Backup JSON for re-importable annotation data, Reviewed Markdown for human-readable review context, and finished delivery artifacts for long-term safekeeping.
support.faqStorageQ: Will my saved work survive clearing browser data?
support.faqStorageA: No. Saved annotations and imported document copies use browser site data. Export Backup JSON and finished review artifacts before clearing site data or moving to another browser, profile, or device.
support.workflowsTitle: Choose the task. Follow the review path.
support.workflowsBody: Each workflow connects a real source, the right review actions, where to focus, and the best delivery artifact.

pro.heroTitle: Review Markdown. Never touch the original.
pro.heroSubtitle: Read any Markdown with structure, record your judgment with four review types, then deliver the right artifact for people, Obsidian, backup, or AI-assisted revision. Local-first and non-destructive.

pro.deliverSubtitle: Share annotated reading with people, send reviewed Markdown to Obsidian, back up your annotations, or hand a precise work order to an AI or editor.
pro.deliverHtmlBody: Self-contained single file preserving structure, outline, highlights, and notes. Offline-readable and opens in any browser.
pro.deliverObsidianBody: A new .md copy with Obsidian-readable review callouts, wowMD tags, and review properties. It does not edit the original or apply suggested replacements.
pro.deliverBackupBody: Raw annotations for backup or re-import. Your data remains portable and under your control.
pro.deliverTicketBody: Document snapshot, bilingual type legend, per-annotation section context, notes, and suggested replacements.
pro.deliverTicketExample:
"type": "dispute"
"headingPath": ["Architecture"]
"note": "This claim needs correction."

Prompt: revise the whole document per these tickets.
pro.versionsTitle: Save an Obsidian-ready Markdown copy without touching the source.
pro.versionsSubtitle: Save reviewed copy creates a new .md file with paragraph-level Obsidian callouts for your wowMD marks, plus review properties and tags. It keeps the original Markdown unchanged; it does not rewrite the document, apply suggested replacements, or call AI.
pro.faqUploadA: No. Files, annotations, versions, and exports are processed in your browser unless you choose to move an exported file elsewhere.
pro.faqDiffQ: How is this different from a Markdown-to-HTML converter?
pro.faqDiffA: A converter only turns Markdown into another format. wowMD Pro is a review layer: read with structure, judge with four semantic types, then deliver HTML for people or a ticket an AI can execute.
pro.faqTicketA: A ticket is a JSON work order built from your annotations: document snapshot, type legend, section context, note, and suggested replacement. Paste it into an AI to revise the document by your judgment.
pro.faqSourceQ: Does wowMD change my source file?
pro.faqSourceA: No. The review is non-destructive. Save reviewed copy creates a separate Markdown file; it does not overwrite the source, apply suggested replacements, or call AI.

support.heroSubtitle: Start with the concepts that make wowMD different: typed review, cross-version survival, reviewed Markdown for Obsidian, and the ticket you can hand to an AI.
support.typedReviewTitle: Typed review: four judgments, not just colors
support.typedReviewBody: When you mark text in wowMD, you record a judgment with an implied action. These types drive the Notes panel, the Overall Review Map, and the Ticket JSON legend.
support.typedReviewClarify: Explain or clarify this point without changing its substance.
support.typedReviewDispute: Review this claim; it may be incorrect and may need correction.
support.typedReviewImportant: Keep and emphasize this key point.
support.typedReviewConfirmed: Reviewed and correct; no action needed.
support.reanchorBody: When the source document changes, wowMD tries to re-anchor your annotations to the same passage using the selected quote and surrounding context. If a passage truly disappears, the mark becomes orphaned and can be recovered manually with Find.
support.reanchorCallout: Re-anchoring is non-destructive. wowMD recalculates annotation positions; it does not write back to the source file.
support.ticketTitle: Ticket JSON: your judgments as an AI work order
support.ticketBody: A ticket bundles the document snapshot, a bilingual type legend, section context, selected quotes, notes, and suggested replacements. It is different from Backup JSON, which stores raw annotations for backup and re-import.
support.ticketStep2: Open your AI tool of choice.
support.ticketStep3: Paste the prompt below, then paste the ticket contents.
support.ticketPrompt:
You are a careful editor. I will give you a JSON ticket of my annotations on a Markdown document.
Handle each entry by its type and output the full revised document.
- clarify: explain or clarify without changing substance
- dispute: review, correct if wrong, and say why
- important: keep and emphasize
- confirmed: leave as is
Use document.markdownSnapshot as the base. Locate each item by headingPath, quote, prefix, and suffix. Prefer suggestedReplacement when provided.
Ticket:
<paste the exported Ticket JSON here>

privacyPage.label: Privacy Policy
privacyPage.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPage.intro: wowMD includes a local-first Chrome extension for reading public GitHub Markdown pages and wowMD Pro, a local-first webapp for reviewing, annotating, and exporting Markdown files.
privacyPage.summaryBody: wowMD does not collect personal information, does not upload documents or annotations, does not sell data, and does not track browsing history. Exports are always initiated by you and generated locally in your browser.
privacyPage.controllerBody: For privacy questions about wowMD, contact the maintainer through the feedback form linked on this website.
privacyPage.dataBody: The extension reads page content locally in your browser only when you choose Better View. wowMD Pro reads local .md files you open and stores the annotations, notes, and suggested replacements you create. Neither product collects account data, cookies, browsing history, or private repository content.
privacyPage.purposeBody: Extension processing is limited to the reading features you request: outline navigation, section folding, code rendering, and table layout. Pro processing is limited to the reviewing features you use: structured reading, four-type annotations, an overall review map, cross-version re-anchoring, and the export formats you choose. Where GDPR applies, this is based on providing the service you request and legitimate interest in operating a privacy-preserving browser tool.
privacyPage.storageBody: wowMD does not maintain a remote database for your reading or reviewing activity. The extension processes pages temporarily within the browser session. wowMD Pro stores your annotations, imported document fingerprints, version history, and settings locally in your browser's site data (IndexedDB). This data is never sent to a wowMD server.
privacyPage.sharingBody: wowMD does not sell or share reading or annotation data. All exports are generated locally in your browser when you initiate them — the resulting files are yours to handle. If you submit feedback through the website, the information you provide, such as your message, feature preferences, and optional email address, is used only to read feedback and follow up on requested features.
privacyPage.webappDataBody: wowMD Pro stores the following data in your browser's site data (IndexedDB), never on a remote server: annotations you create (type, note, suggested replacement, context), document fingerprints used for cross-version re-anchoring, imported document copies for review, version history, and your preferences (theme, font size, layout). This data stays in your browser unless you choose to export it.
privacyPage.exportPrivacyBody: All exports are generated locally in your browser when you initiate them. HTML export includes rendered Markdown with your highlights and notes visible. Reviewed Markdown includes your annotations as Obsidian callouts in a new .md file. Backup JSON contains your raw annotation data for backup or re-import. Ticket JSON includes a full document snapshot, your annotations, and section context — review this content before sharing it with an AI or third party.
privacyPage.googleTitle: Chrome Web Store and Limited Use
privacyPage.googleBody: wowMD uses browser permissions only to provide the disclosed reading features. Information received from Google APIs, if any, will be used in accordance with the Chrome Web Store User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements.
privacyPage.rightsBody: Depending on your location, including the European Economic Area, you may have rights to access, correct, delete, restrict, object to, or port personal data. Because wowMD does not store reading or annotation data on a server, most requests can be answered by explaining what is and is not collected.
privacyPage.childrenBody: wowMD is not directed to children and does not knowingly collect personal information from children.
privacyPage.changesBody: If wowMD changes its data practices, this policy will be updated before those changes are released.
termsPage.label: Terms and Conditions
termsPage.title: Terms and Conditions
termsPage.intro: These terms explain how you may use the wowMD website, Chrome extension, and wowMD Pro webapp.
termsPage.summaryBody: Use wowMD responsibly, keep your own documents safe, and do not misuse the service. The free Chrome extension and wowMD Pro webapp are provided as focused Markdown reading and reviewing tools. Both are free during beta.
termsPage.acceptanceBody: By using the wowMD website, extension, or webapp, you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, do not use wowMD.
termsPage.productsBody: wowMD includes a free Chrome extension for supported public GitHub Markdown pages, and wowMD Pro, a local-first webapp for local Markdown reading, four-type annotations, an overall review map, cross-version re-anchoring, and four export formats (HTML, Reviewed Markdown for Obsidian, Backup JSON, Ticket JSON). Both are free during beta. Features may change as the product evolves.
termsPage.licenseBody: wowMD Pro is free during beta. Future paid access, if introduced, will be described on the relevant checkout or product page. Do not share, resell, or abuse license keys or access credentials.
termsPage.pricingBody: wowMD Pro is free during beta. If paid access is introduced later, exact prices, discounts, taxes, currency, and payment terms will be shown at checkout or on the relevant purchase page. Free beta access does not guarantee that the product will remain free permanently.
termsPage.localBody: You are responsible for the Markdown files, annotations, notes, reviewed copies, and exports you open or create with wowMD. The app processes documents and annotations locally in your browser using site data storage (IndexedDB). wowMD does not modify your source files or apply suggested replacements. You should keep backups of important files, annotations, and exported content. Clearing your browser's site data, using private browsing, or browser storage eviction may result in data loss.
termsPage.exportsBody: wowMD Pro provides four export formats, all generated locally in your browser: (1) HTML — a self-contained file with structure, highlights, and notes, for sharing annotated reading with people; (2) Reviewed Markdown — a new .md copy with Obsidian-readable review callouts, tags, and properties, without modifying the original file; (3) Backup JSON — raw annotation data for backup or re-import, fully portable under your control; (4) Ticket JSON — a document snapshot, type legend, section context, notes, and suggested replacements packaged as a work order for AI-assisted revision. Exports are your responsibility once you download or share them.
termsPage.dataLossBody: wowMD Pro stores annotations, document fingerprints, imported document copies, version history, and preferences in your browser's site data (IndexedDB). This data is local to your browser and is not synced across devices or backed up to a server. Clearing your browser's site data, switching to a different browser or profile, using private/incognito windows, or browser storage pressure eviction may permanently delete your annotations and version history. Export a Backup JSON regularly to protect your work.
termsPage.betaBody: wowMD Pro is provided free during its beta period. Beta access may include incomplete features, changes without notice, and the possibility of data incompatibility between versions. Free beta access does not guarantee the product will remain free, that features will be preserved, or that beta-era data will be compatible with post-beta releases. We advise exporting Backup JSON copies of your annotations regularly.
termsPage.allowedBody: Do not use wowMD to break the law, infringe others' rights, attack or disrupt services, bypass technical limits, reverse engineer paid access controls, or interfere with other users.
termsPage.thirdPartyBody: wowMD may link to third-party services such as Chrome Web Store, GitHub, payment providers, feedback forms, or video hosts. Those services are governed by their own terms and policies.
termsPage.openSourceBody: The wowMD extension may be distributed with open source code or dependencies. Open source licenses continue to apply to those parts. These terms do not remove rights granted by an applicable open source license.
termsPage.disclaimerBody: wowMD is provided as is and as available. We do not promise that every Markdown file, export, browser, store listing, reader, or device will work perfectly or without interruption.
termsPage.liabilityBody: To the maximum extent permitted by law, wowMD and its maintainers are not liable for indirect, incidental, special, consequential, or lost-profit damages arising from your use of the product.
termsPage.changesBody: We may update these terms when the product, licensing, payment flow, or legal requirements change. The updated terms will be posted on this page with a new update date.
termsPage.contactBody: For questions about these terms, contact the maintainer through the feedback form linked on this website.
